Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
1250 AM EST Sat Nov 28 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes made to the forecast with this update.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Breezy with seasonable temperatures through Saturday. 

2) A frontal system will bring another chance of rain to the
area late Sunday night into Monday, with gusty winds on Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Low pressure over far upstate NY will deepen some while passing
north through Saturday. At the same time, high pressure will
gradually build from the south and west through Sunday morning.
This will maintain a sufficient pressure gradient across the 
area for gusty winds to continue, veering from the SW to W 
overnight. Gusts will be highest near the coast at 20-30 mph, 
strongest during the daytime hours. In addition, with deep layer
cyclonic flow, expect plenty of clouds but with breaks at 
times. Skies will clear from SW to NW late Saturday afternoon 
into the evening.

Gusty winds and clouds will limit radiational cooling tonight, 
with lows mainly around 40. Highs Saturday will be in the lower
50s. This is slightly above normal for highs, but about 5-8
degrees above normal for lows. 

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
High pressure on Sunday will give way to an approaching frontal
system, with a slightly warmer day and less wind. Amplifying
Pacific jet energy will carve out a deepening upper trough over
the Mississippi Valley on Sunday. There is some interaction with
the northern branch of the polar jet, with even a slight 
negative tilt as the upper trough approaches the eastern 
seaboard Monday morning. This will result in a rapidly deepening
low passing to our north and a period of moderate rain along 
and ahead of the cold front. The system is progressive enough at
this time that rainfall amounts are forecast at 1/2 inch or 
less. Much of the rain will be over by afternoon. South winds 
ahead the system will ramp up Sunday night, veering to the W on 
Monday, with potential gusts of 30-40 mph. There is a chance to 
meet marginal wind advisory criteria. Winds will then gradually 
subside Monday night.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
The terminals will remain between departing low pressure and high 
pressure to the south.

Mainly VFR overnight. Cigs should lower to MVFR during the daylight 
hours, and return to VFR tonight. Exceptions to this are KGON which 
should remain VFR, and KBDR which should have limited MVFR cigs in 
the afternoon. 

High confidence in WSW flow 10-15 kt with gusts 20-25 kt, though 
some outlying terminals should diminish to 10 kt with occasional 
gusts 15-20 kt overnight until around 13Z-14Z. 

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Unscheduled amendments possible only if cigs lower to MVFR sooner 
than fcst. There is also the chance that cigs remain VFR for
most of the daylight hours.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Sunday through Wednesday... 

Late tonight: VFR with diminishing W flow. 

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night and Monday: Rain likely with MVFR or lower cond
after midnight through early Monday morning. Rain could persist
E of the NYC metro terminals after sunrise, but improving cond
likely through the day. S winds G20-30 kt late Sunday night with
a few hours of LLWS possible, then W winds G25-35 kt on Monday.
Winds diminish Monday night.

Tuesday and Wednesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SW-W gales will continue on much of the ocean tonight, with the
exception of Sandy Hook to Fire Island Inlet out 20 nm. 
Even that zone may see a few gusts hit 35 kt, but most gusts 
should generally closer to 30 kt. Ocean seas at 8-12 ft from 
Sandy Hook to Fire Island Inlet out 20 nm, and 11-17 south and 
east of there, will gradually subside through Sunday. 

With deepening low pressure passing to the north tonight into
Saturday. SCA cond are expected across all waters Saturday and
on the ocean into Saturday night, before winds and seas subside
below criteria. High pressure will briefly build across late
Saturday night into Sunday, followed by a strong frontal system
with potential for gales late Sunday night into Mon.
